info.name: OAN Grievance Service REST API
info.description: Postman collection for OpenAgriNet Grievance Management Module REST routing API endpoints (/v1/...) covering health, public reference metadata, authentication, submitter profile lookups, draft save/resume, grievance intake, listing with multi-select filters, tracking, timeline, notes, reply, escalation, resolution confirmation, reopen flows, category-assignment admin CRUD, and the read-only Review Officer role.

item.name: 0. Full Happy Path (E2E Runner)
item.description: Self-contained, order-dependent smoke flow. Needs only 3 starting credentials: base_url, admin_email, admin_password (all collection variables). Logs in as admin; creates a fresh service category, grievance type, department (via L3 head), L1 officer, category assignment; registers a farmer; submits a grievance; officer resolves; farmer reopens it (only valid from Resolved -- once Closed the case is final and a new grievance must be filed instead); officer resolves again; farmer closes for good. Run top-to-bottom with Collection Runner / newman against a site with `bench worker` running (first auto-route after submit is a background queue job).

request.description:
Serve the bytes of one attachment for display in the browser.

The private-file route that `file_url` points at sits outside the JWT
namespaces, so a bearer token does nothing there and a Next.js client cannot
open the URL it was handed. This route is under `/v1`, so the same token
that listed the case also fetches the file, and the scan gate is applied on
the way out. Inline by default so an image or PDF opens in the tab; pass
`download=1` for a Save As.

item.name: SLA Settings
item.description: STG-412 admin API for the SLA tab: the global SLA policy and the per-category SLA windows. Per-category sla_days and auto_escalate are the same values as Category Assignments. Writes need a Grievance Admin or System Manager bearer token.

request.description: Installation-wide policy: max_deferral_days and requires_supervisor_approval (true: a senior officer decides a deferral; false: the assigned officer may approve it).
Send either field or both; omitted fields stay as they are.

The SLA rules, by service category and then oldest first. Filter by service_category (id, name or code), grievance_type, administrative_area, is_urgent or is_base. Every rule sets sla_days and is_urgent for the cases it matches on their filing date; an urgent rule gives the case priority Urgent, any other rule no priority (priority is read only). A rule may name a grievance_type of its category, an administrative_area (covering the areas inside it) and a recurring window (start_month, start_day, end_month, end_day: all four, or none for all year; a start after the end wraps the year end, for example 10/1 to 4/30). The category's base rule (is_base) names none of them: it is the category's SLA wherever no narrower rule matches, a category needs it before any other rule, and it cannot be deleted or narrowed. The most specific matching rule wins: a type's rule before the category's, a narrower area before a wider one, a windowed rule before an all-year one. Two windowed rules, or two all-year rules, for the same type and area may not share a day. A change applies to cases filed afterwards.

Add one rule to a service category. service_category and sla_days are required; is_urgent defaults to false (true makes the case Urgent, with priority Urgent). priority is not sent: it follows is_urgent. A category's first rule must be its base rule (no type, area or window); creating a category with sla_days, or setting sla_days on /sla-configurations, makes it. item.name: Service Categories & Grievance Types
item.description: STG-406 admin CRUD for the service categories and grievance types the submission wizard, category assignments and response templates share. Requires a Grievance Admin or System Manager bearer token for writes; Grievance Review Officer may read. Records are retired, never deleted.

request.description: List categories in display order, active and inactive. Optional query: is_active, search (name or code), page, page_size. Each record counts the active types, assignments and templates that refer to it. Unknown query parameters return 400. Grievance Review Officer may call this.

Create a category. Required: category_name, code. The code is the 3-character ticket segment, in the ticket alphabet (no I, L, O or U), and unique. sort_order is optional and defaults to the end of the list; is_active defaults to true. is_default (default false) true makes this the category unclassified cases fall to and clears the flag on the previous default; it needs is_active true. Optional sla_days, auto_escalate, and notify_on_breach establish the category's SLA configuration atomically. Duplicate name or code returns 409.
One category, by name or ticket code. 404 when unknown.

Partial update of category_name, code, sort_order, is_active or is_default. Renaming keeps every grievance, type, routing rule, SLA row and template linked and runs in the background: the response keeps the old category_name and shows renaming_to until the job is done, then the category answers to the new name. The code cannot change once tickets exist (code_locked). Setting is_active false also deactivates its types, and is refused for the default category. is_default true makes this the default (the previous default loses the flag); false is refused because exactly one category must be the default.

Make this the default category: the one cases with no category (an IVR call or email that named none, a draft saved without a choice) are filed under. The previous default loses the flag, and the new default gets an active catch-all Other type if it has none. The category must be active. Send the same request for another category to move the default; is_default false is refused.

Retire the category and its types (refused for the default category: make another the default first). Nothing is deleted: grievances keep them and the submission dropdowns stop offering them. Routing rules and templates already set up on the category stay active for open cases. Same as PATCH with is_active false; repeating the call changes nothing.

List types by category and name, active and inactive. Optional query: service_category (name or code), is_active, search (text in the type name), page, page_size. Unknown query parameters return 400. Grievance Review Officer may call this.

Create a type under an active category. Required: service_category (name or code), type_name. The name is unique within the category (the same name under another category is allowed). Duplicate returns 409.
One type, by grievance_type_id. 404 when unknown.

Partial update of type_name or is_active. The service category cannot change. A type cannot be reactivated while its category is inactive, and the catch-all Other type of the default category cannot be deactivated.
Retire the type. Grievances keep it and the submission dropdowns stop offering it. Same as PATCH with is_active false; repeating the call changes nothing.

item.name: Officers
item.description: STG-430 admin CRUD for officers, extended by STG-443. An officer is a User placed on category desks, so the id is the officer's email and every service category must already have a category assignment for the department. level is L1 (Nodal), L2 (Senior Nodal) or L3 (Category Admin, the Admin tab). role is Officer (default) or Reviewer: a Reviewer is placed on the department's desks with read-only access to that department and is never assigned a case. Requires a Grievance Admin bearer token. Accounts are deactivated by updating status, not deleted. Performance metrics come from the statistics API.

request.description: Filter by role (Officer by default, or Reviewer), level (L1/L2/L3), department, status, service_category, region (exact area), or search text q. level L3 lists the department heads. A Reviewer has no level, so level and status On Leave return 400 with role=Reviewer. Paginated with page and page_size; the pagination block is at the top level of the response.
Create a Senior Nodal (L2) officer. The email must already have a login (create it first with POST /v1/users).
Create a Nodal (L1) officer. reports_to is an L2 officer id (their email) and is only valid for an L1. The email must already have a login.

Reissue a temporary password to an existing officer, for example after a forgotten password. Their sessions end at once and they must replace the password through POST /v1/auth/password/initial before signing in. Refused for an account that holds an admin role.
Fetch one officer, department head or Reviewer by email, with the desks (RBAC assignments) they sit on.
Move an officer between L1 and L2. The move clears their supervisor, and an L2 with L1 officers reporting to them cannot change level.
Partial update. service_categories replaces the whole list and re-seats the officer on those desks. Send phone, region or reports_to as null to clear them. email is rejected.
Deactivation is a status update: Active, On Leave or Inactive. On Leave skips auto-routing; Inactive also retires the officer's desk rows.

Active, On Leave, Inactive and total counts for the officers tabs, with the same filters as the list but no status. Each person is counted once, by the most available of their desk rows. The UI shows these in place of its hardcoded counts.
The Admin tab: department heads (level L3), optionally for one department.

Create a department head. level L3 places the head on the department's desks for the given categories as its final escalation rung. They approve the department's reassignments and are not assigned first-line cases. reports_to is not accepted.
Reviewers, by name. Needs an admin role.

Place a Reviewer on a department's desks. department and service_categories are required; level and reports_to are refused. The login gets the Grievance Review Officer role and reads only those desks' cases. A Reviewer is never assigned a case and cannot change one.
A Reviewer has no level or supervisor. The response is 400 VALIDATION_ERROR and details names each field.
Change a Reviewer's name, designation, phone, region, department or service categories. level and reports_to return 400.
status Inactive retires the Reviewer's desk rows, disables their login and ends their sessions and refresh tokens, so they cannot sign in. On Leave returns 400.
status Active enables the login and the desk rows again. The password is unchanged.

item.name: Export a grievance and its timeline as the SOW Annexure form (CSV or PDF)

query.description: File format of the exported form

request.description:
Download one grievance, with its timeline, laid out as the SOW Annexure complaint form.

`format` is `pdf` (default) or `csv`. The role check (the Grievance `export` permission)
and the case check are made here, in that order, and the file holds only what the caller
may already read on the case: staff get internal notes and officer names, a submitter the
public record, and an anonymous submitter's identity stays sealed. Every attempt, allowed,
refused or failed, is written to the access audit trail.

The body is the file itself, not the JSON envelope; errors use the envelope.

item.name: View a sensitive anonymous grievance with its link and PIN

request.description:
Check the ticket and token from the link and the PIN typed, and return that one case.

Read-only and stateless: send all three on every view. A wrong ticket, token or PIN all answer
401 `GUEST_ACCESS_INVALID`. With the right link, too many wrong PINs answer 429
`GUEST_ACCESS_LOCKED` (with `retry_after_seconds`) until the lock ends, and a closed case
answers 410 `GUEST_ACCESS_CLOSED` once the PIN is right. 503 `GUEST_ACCESS_UNAVAILABLE` when
the site is not configured for it.
